fidelityScope: The three inspected primary Alien: Isolation images support materials, construction and palette. Asphodele is an original project station. Room assemblies follow the existing project slots, not a claimed canonical location or a certified 1:1 film/game frame reproduction.
compositionPolicy: Opaque orthographic back-wall images, no gameplay doorway, no freestanding interactive foreground object. Separate native doors/posts/actors remain above the wall. Background equipment and lamps are static dressing, not indicators of live game state.
pixelPolicy: Selected generated PNGs copied byte-for-byte; no bitmap crop, resize, recolour, re-encode or other pixel edit. Canvas uses uniform scale at height 504, world origin x0 and a cached repeat-x pattern, clipped to the existing world span.
generatedRatioPolicy: Requested 1280:504; actual returned image dimensions differ slightly. Their actual aspect ratios are preserved in game; no stretch to requested width.

assets.prompt:
Create one finished raster BACK WALL asset for the side-view 2D game Aliens: Tantalus Frontier, Asphodèle station. The supplied reference images are MATERIAL AND CONSTRUCTION references from the actual Alien: Isolation art director portfolio; adapt their faithfully observed retro-industrial Alien construction, never their first-person camera or HUD. Asphodèle is an original project setting.
CRITICAL projection: a perfectly flat orthographic architectural FRONT ELEVATION of one long back wall, every wall panel parallel to the image plane. No vanishing point, no corridor receding into depth, no isometric or 3/4 view, no visible side wall, no floor or ceiling plane. Very wide canvas aspect ratio EXACTLY1280:504 (approximately2.54:1), preferably2560x1008. The rectangular wall fills the entire canvas edge to edge, fully opaque, NO border, no transparency, no title, no margins.
The wall is a horizontally repeatable module. Both vertical edge strips have matching plain dark structural metal with identical height and illumination; horizontal pipes continue level across opposite edges. Broad diffuse lighting uniform left to right, no spotlight falloff at the edges. Native gameplay will draw the walkable floor directly below the bottom edge, so bottom is a straight flush wall skirting, no objects extending below it.
Practical late-1970s physical construction: weathered dirty ivory panels, graphite steel, warm brown rubber padding, ribbed conduits, mechanical clamps, bolts and thick molded bevels. Detailed realistic game texture, sharply legible, restrained scuffs and wear; shadow relief is shallow. No cartoon, no vector, no colored outline, no glossy futuristic holograms, no blue neon, no cinematic fog or lens effects.
DO NOT draw any DOOR, doorway, open archway, airlock aperture, window into space, person, creature, vehicle, freestanding interactive object, floor clutter or furniture projecting into the play space. Actual doors and props are separate game sprites. No lettering, words, numbers, signs with text, logos, pseudo-writing or symbols. Empty nameplate/monitor surfaces only. No hazard stripe at the wall base: the game draws the live hazard strip separately. Do not reproduce watermarks or labels from the references.
SUBJECT AND LOCAL VARIATION: Docking quay service back wall. Heavy broad bolted dark steel plates and thick riveted structural uprights, low-pressure utility junction boxes, small blank recessed dark green CRT housings up high, chunky hose guides and horizontal black cable runs. Muted ochre safety-painted fasteners as small accents, charcoal and warm industrial grey dominant. The station side of the docking collars is represented by solid machinery support plating ONLY, with absolutely no painted collar circles or openings; the real docking doors are drawn later. Calm, robust, used working harbor wall. A very thin horizontal top cable ledge, repeated practical panel rhythm across the width.
assets.slotPurpose: Docking quays: the station side of the docking collars.
assets.originalSlotBrief: Back wall of a profile room, 1280 × 504 px above the floor line (y 120 → 624), tileable horizontally, no door drawn (doors are their own slot). Reference cited, not copied: the hangar and airlock look of Sevastopol in Alien: Isolation (2014) — heavy riveted plating, yellow-black hazard bands, CRT status boxes beside each collar. Project design: Asphodèle is a Seegson relay station (bible §7.1); three numbered collars.
